D.S.I. Gigarson.

Sir,

In furtherance to enquiries in the strike of 60
workmen at Liddell Brothers & Co. Ltd, 248 Yangtszepoo
Road the undersigned begs to report that an understanding
was reached between the management of the above firm
with the workmen upon which, owing to decline in business,
20 workmen were dismissed and 40 workmen resumed work
at 6 a.m. on the 25.11.40, with no increase in pay.

It is understood that the 20 dismissed workmen were
only recently engaged and actually were responsible for
the strike, whilst the 40 old hands joined in rather
unwillingly.

No political motive is suspected and no further
trouble expected.

INDUSTRIAL DISPUTE.

Some 26 workers employed in the Press Packing Works
of Messrs. Liddell Bros. & Co., Ltd. 248 Yangtszepoo Road,
requested the Management on September 2nd, 1940 to grant a
food allowance of $10 each per month.

The Industrial Section representative was asked by
Mr. J. H. Liddell, Managing Director, to attend a consultation
at his office, 4 Peking Road, at 11 a.m. September 3rd. Mr.
Liddell stated that the workers in the Press Packing Works were
treated exactly the same as those in other departments. Their
basic wages ranged from $33 to $42 per month, plus 40 per cent.
H.C.L. allowance and $6 each per month, besides a rice allow-
ance of $9.45 for June, $17.70 for July and $15.45 for August.
Thus the average monthly earnings came to more than $72 per
month. He requested the Industrial Section representative to
make a study of the matter before further allowances were con-
sidered.

The Industrial Section representative proceeded to
the Works, 248 Yangtszepoo Road, at 2.30 p.m. the same day to
make enquiries. After an interview with the foreman, Ling
Tsen Tang (林填堂), and other workers, it was learned that
they wanted the Management to provide hot rice at noon, as was
done in the Casablancas Factory of the same Company, or, as
an alternative, $10 cash each per month as a food allowance.

After consultation with Mr. Liddell, the latter
agreed to provide hot rice daily at tiffin time for the 26
workers in the Press Packing Works, and said he would consider
similar treatment for the other 34 woolies in the godown.

The Industrial Section representative proceeded once
more to the Works, and conveyed to the workers the Management's
decision. The workers were satisfied with this arrangement, and
the dispute was settled without the occurrence of a strike.

POSSIBLE SOLUTION OF LABOUR TROUBLE IN LIDDELL
BROTHERS & CO.

The workers of Liddell Brothers &
Co. have submitted the following three demands:-

(1) 25% increase of wages.
(2) Immediate reinstatement of dismissed workers.
(3) Full pay for the period of the strike.
The company has accepted the first
and the second demands. As regard demand No. 3, the
Company offers to pay only two day's wages instead of
seven days.

However, it is probable that the trouble will be
settled soon

COLLECTIVE AGREEMENT MADE BETWEEN
THE WORKERS & THE MANAGEMENT OF
CASABLANCAS FACTORY OF LIDDELL BROTHERS & CO.,LTD.

1. The management will grant an increase of 10 cents per day
in wages to all workers. But the management will cancel
5 cents at the end of December, 1939 out of the 20 cents
rice allowance which has been issued by the management.
The remaining rice allowance shall be cancelled according
to the following rice prices:

a. If the price of second grade rice is below $17,
allowance shall be lessened by 5 cents.
b. If the price of second grade rice is below $15,
allowance shall be lessened by 10 cents.
c. If the price of second grade rice is below $12,
the whole allowance shall be cancelled.

2. The 15 workers who have been dismissed by the management
shall be reinstated on the date of resuming work.

3. The management will pay two days' wages each to all workers
for time lost during the strike.

4. The fluting tools which have been stolen shall be returned
by the workers after investigation. The workers who were
arrested by the police if they are not guilty of any theft
shall be compensated by the management.

5. New factory regulations to be drawn shall be approved by
the Industrial Section, S. M. C.

6. All the workers shall resume work on November 6, 1939.

以下是工人提出的要求：

pages.en:
Conditions suggested by the Management are
as follows :
(1) That investigations be made by both parties
concerned in connection with the property
(fluting tools) stolen from the company.
(2) That the workers' union be dissolved.
(3) That the foremen be held responsible for
the future conduct of workers.
(4) That the foremen be held responsible for
the daily manufacture of the company stocks
being kept in order.
(5) That advertisements be inserted in the local
newspapers stating that the Management is in
no way at fault regarding the present labour
dispute.
(6) That all workers observe the new factory rules
which are put in force by the management.
(7) That work be resumed on November 2, if an
agreement can be reached in respect of the
above conditions.

管理层建议的条件如下：
(1) 有关双方应对公司被盗财产（压花工具）进行调查。
(2) 解散工人工会。
(3) 领班须对工人未来的行为负责。
(4) 领班须对公司库存的日常生产保持有序负责。
(5) 在当地报纸上刊登广告，声明管理层对本次劳资纠纷没有任何过错。
(6) 所有工人须遵守管理层实施的新工厂规则。
(7) 如果就上述条件达成协议，则于11月2日复工。

pages.en:
The following concessions were made by
the Management in connection with the workers'
demands :

(1) That the workers would be granted a 5%
wage increase.
(2) That no dismissed workers would be reinstated.
(3) That the workers would be paid four days'
wages for the period of the strike.
(4) That a statement confirming the innocence
of the two workers arrested for theft would
be made after the case had been cleared up.
pages.zh:

(1) 给予工人5%的工资增加。

INDUSTRIAL DISPUTE

The strike of the workers employed in Casablanca
Factory of Liddell Brothers & Company, 248 Yangtszepoo Road,
continues to-day, November 3, 1939.

The No.1 foreman, Chen Tsang Ling (陈长林), reported
through the telephone at 9:30 this morning, that the Workers'
Representatives are willing to have the Industrial Section
mediate the dispute and will meet at 10:30 a.m. at Great Eastern
Tea Room, 635 Nanking Road. Through the introduction of the
foreman, I met the Workers' Representatives at the above place.
After persuasion, the Workers' Representatives agreed to reduce
their demand for an increase to 10 cents per day in wages, and
including demands already agreed upon by the representatives of
both parties on October 31, 1939. Then I brought the minimum
demand of the workers with six foremen to see Messrs. R. W. Fraser
and Chu Chi Hsing at 11:30 a.m. at the factory, 248 Yangtszepoo
Road. The management refused to consider any increase in wages
or to reinstate the fifteen dismissed workers at present, since
the workers refused to accept the management's offer of November
2. After careful consideration, Messrs. Fraser & Chu promised to
grant an increase of 10 cents per day in wages but will cancel
the 5 cents of the 20 cents daily rice allowance which has been
granted by the management in June 1939. Other demands which have
been agreed between the two parties on October 31, will be
accepted as a final settlement.

I met the workers' representatives together with six
foremen at 2:30 this afternoon, at Great Eastern Tea Room. After
negotiation, the representatives of the workers and of the
management, Mr. Chu Chi Hsing, finally agreed to the following
terms as drafted by the Industrial Section representative.

1. The management will grant an increase of 10 cents
per day in wages to all workers. But the management
will cancel 5 cents at the end of December, 1939
out of the 20 cents rice allowance which has been

hitherto granted daily to the employees be

(2) That the fifteen dismissed workers be reinstated
when the company resumes operations.

(3) That the workers be paid two days' wages for
the period of the strike.

(4) That the fluting tools stolen from the company
be returned to the management when they are
found by the workers, and that compensation be
granted to the two suspects if they are found
not guilty of theft.

(5) That the new factory regulations be issued after
approval by the Industrial Section of the S.M.C.

1.11.29 (PM)
SERIOUS DEVELOPMENTS EXPECTED IN LIDDELL BROTHERS
STRIKE

Following the strike on October 24, the
workers of Liddell Brothers & Co. organized a body
consisting of 150 persons. On October 25, demands were
submitted to the management by this body and at the same
time letters were delivered to various circles in
Shanghai explaining their attitude. However, the
management of the company has still not changed its
coercive attitude, ignoring entirely the demands made
by the workers. As a consequence, those who were
dissatisfied by the highly oppressive attitude of the
management have now also joined the protesting body with
the object of fighting against the capitalistic party
to the end.
The state of affairs at present is very
serious. In case the management fails to show a
sincere attitude, an exceedingly serious outcome will
likely ensue within the next few days.

STRIKE SITUATION AT LIDDELL BROTHERS BECOMES WORSE

It is reported that 150 workers of
Liddell Brothers on Yangtszepoo Road, who went on strike
on October 24, presented a number of demands to the
management of the factory on October 25 and issued a
manifesto to justify their action.
As a result of the oppressive measures
adopted by the management against the strikers, the other
workers of the factory are now reported to be joining the
strike thereby aggravating the situation.
Should the management fail to adopt
a sincere attitude towards the strikers in two or three
days, serious consequences are expected.

Strikers Demands met as follows:-
(1) Further increase of 25% of our daily wages.
(2) To resume the work of those fifteen dismissed workers.
(3) Pay back the wages during the period of strike.
(4) Two men arrested by police, compensation if not guilty

(1) Fluting tools to be returned, no questions asked.
(2) Liddell Bros & Co. Workers Union to be dissolved and any
worker of any other Union to resign from such Union.
(3) Future behaviour of workers to be guaranteed.

罢工解决：

罢工者的要求得到如下满足：-
(1) 我们的日工资进一步增加25%。
(2) 恢复那十五名被解雇工人的工作。

(4) 两名被警察逮捕的人，若无任何盗窃罪行，则给予赔偿。

(2) 解散利德尔兄弟公司工人工会，任何其他工会的工人须退出该工会。
(3) 保证工人未来的行为。
(4) 保证生产。

The labour dispute between the workers and
management of Liddell Brothers Company, 248
Yangtszepoo Road, remains unsettled.
During the afternoon of October 31, a meeting
was held in Room 311, Ming Saung Lodging House, 469
Tientsin Road, when one ZUNG TSANG LING (陈亭林),
foreman of the Liddell Brothers Company and two
labour delegates named TSAI CHING FOH (张庆福)
and YOUNG AH YUN (熊阿元) were present.
The following demands were put forward by the
workers representatives :
(1) That the workers be granted a flat wage
increase of 20%.
(2) That the fifteen dismissed workers be reinstated.
(3) That the workers be paid for the period of the
strike.
(4) That the management give an announcement to the
workers to assert the good conduct of the two
workers who were arrested by the Municipal
Police on suspicion of being guilty of theft
and later released.
These demands were communicated by the
foreman to the management, who agreed to accept
Nos.2 and 4 demands but rejected the other two
demands.
The management further suggested the
following conditions to the workers :
(1) That the workers be held responsible for the
discovery and return of the property stolen
from the factory.
(2) That no labour unions or organizations of a
similar nature be formed.

位于杨树浦路248号的利德尔兄弟公司工人与管理方之间的劳资纠纷仍未解决。
10月31日下午，在天津路469号明松旅馆（Ming Saung Lodging House，音译）311室举行了一次会议，利德尔兄弟公司领班陈亭林（ZUNG TSANG LING，注：原文拼音与中文名对应可能有误，依原文译出）以及两名名为张庆福（TSAI CHING FOH）和熊阿元（YOUNG AH YUN）的劳工代表出席。
工人代表提出了以下要求：
(1) 工人工资统一增加20%。
(2) 复职十五名被解雇的工人。
(3) 支付罢工期间的工人工资。
(4) 管理方向工人发布公告，申明两名因涉嫌盗窃被捕后获释的工人行为良好。
这些要求由领班传达给管理方，管理方同意接受第2和第4项要求，但拒绝了其他两项要求。
管理方进一步向工人提出以下条件：
(1) 工人须负责找回并归还从工厂被盗的财产。
(2) 不得成立工会或类似性质的组织。

The workers of the Liddell

At 10.30 a.m. on the 27.10.39 the management received
a letter from the Tung Ming Hwei (同盟会), Pootung.
(Chinese Republic Workers League) delivered by a coolie.
The envelope - ill-destroyed by recipient - was addressed
to Mr. Ts Ching Sing (朱敬新) the Chinese manager,
Messrs. Liddell Brothers., The contents read as follows:-

" Mr. Ching Sing,
It is quite unpleasant to mention
that the present strike is resultant from an
alleged theft said to have taken place on the
19th. Inst. in the machine shop.
We should say that we have no
grievance between the management and labourers,
even though our friends the workers were compelled
by you to leave the factory. However, they are
earnestly expecting to reach an early reasonable
settlement of the strike.
We wonder if there is any channel
open by which you will care to negotiate direct
with the workers. If so, please send a represen-
tative with sole power to act on your behalf and
make the necessary arrangements for an appointment.
Please give your reply to bearer.

From all workers.
27.10.39. "

The bearer was not detained by the management nor
was this fact on informed until this morning. However, the
management have ignored the contents of their first demand.

At 1 p.m. 27.10.39 more than fifty workers returned,
at 7 a.m. this morning seventy eight or more returned.
From continued enquiries it would seem the Police action
on the morning of the 27.10.39, that none of the dismissed
employees are to be seen in this area North of the Creek.
It is presumed that they are now either in Pootung or
South of the Creek, and as a consequence the more loyal of
the workers may now return assured of no outside inter-

“敬新先生：
提及此事颇令人不快，目前的罢工据称是由于本月19日在机器车间发生的一起盗窃案所致。
我们要说，尽管我们的工人朋友被迫离开工厂，但我们与管理层和劳工之间并无怨隙。然而，他们殷切期望能早日合理解决罢工问题。
我们想知道是否有渠道可以让您直接与工人进行谈判。如果有，请派遣一位拥有全权代表您行事能力的代表，并安排会面事宜。
请给送信人答复。

全体工人。
1939年10月27日。”

送信人未被管理层扣留，且直到今晨才将此事实告知警方。然而，管理层无视了他们第一份要求的内容。

My name is SONG TSUNG SAN. I am 23 years of
age, a native of Ningpo, married and residing at 78 Shou
Ping Li, Ward Road. I am an ex-employee of Liddell
Brothers Company, 248 Yangtszepoo Road.

In May, 1937, I joined Liddell Brothers Company
as Fitter No.25 and received $1.40 a day. During the
early part of September, 1939, I applied for leave of
absence, but failed to return on the date due. I was
therefore dismissed.

On September 14, 1939, I was asked by two
ex-fitters of the same company named WOO LING YUIN
( 吳林雲 ) and SHIH CHIEN YING ( 石泉榮 ) to join
the Chinese Republic Workers' League ( 中華民國工人同盟會 )
situated on Tung Chong Road, Pootung. The Chairman of
the league is a Korean named LING TSE CHUN ( 林資炯 )
and the Chinese leaders are KOO CHING KENG ( 顧金根 )
and one named CHOW ( 周 ), two ex-workers of the China
Printing and Finishing Company, Pootung. I was not
required to pay any membership fee and on the contrary
the league issued me with allowances from time to time.
Up to the present, I received a total of $14 from the
league. At the beginning of October I received $5, ten
days later $5 more and ten days later $4.

On the morning of October 24, a strike broke out
in the Liddell Brothers Company. On October 25, another
ex-worker of the company named JU CHING KENG ( 瞿金根 )
alias TAI PAO AN SZ ( 太保阿書 ) instructed me while I was

1937年5月，我加入利德尔兄弟公司，担任25号装配工，日薪1.40元。1939年9月上旬，我申请休假，但未按期返岗。因此被解雇。

1939年9月14日，该公司两名前装配工吴林云（WOO LING YUIN）和石泉荣（SHIH CHIEN YING）邀我加入位于浦东东昌路的中华民国工人同盟会。该会主席为一名朝鲜人林资炯（LING TSE CHUN），中方领导人为顾金根（KOO CHING KENG）和一名姓周（CHOW）的人，此二人均为浦东中国印刷整理公司的前工人。我不需缴纳任何会费，相反，该会不时向我发放津贴。截至目前，我从该会共收到14元。10月初收到5元，十天后又收到5元，再十天后收到4元。

10月24日上午，利德尔兄弟公司爆发罢工。10月25日，该公司另一名前工人瞿金根（JU CHING KENG），别名太保阿书（TAI PAO AN SZ），指示我在

workers had already entered but we succeeded in preventing
the other workers from proceeding to work.

The pickets included the leader JU CHING KENG
alias TAI PAO AH SZ, LI MIAO KWEI (李妙柜) and CHANG

Company, and YING SHOU LING (殷寿林), CHANG CHING KENG
(张金柜), SHUN MUR (成茂) and KONG MAO KENG
(康毛柜), who are strikers. After completing our
picketing work, we departed en route to our home via
Wayside Road, where detectives attached to Wayside Police
Station arrested me.

My name is Chang Ching-keng (張金根). I
am 18 years of age, a native of Sungkiang, single and
residing at 29 Yung Jen Fang (永仁坊), Dalny Road. I
am a blacksmith in the employ of Biddell Brothers Company,
248 Yangtszepoo Road, where I have been working for six
months.

At 5 p.m. September 17, when the workers left
the company premises, ex-fitters named Woo Ling-yuin
(吳林芳), Shih Chien-yung (石建榮) and Chang Ching-foh (張金福)
approached us and led us to the Chinese Republic Labourers'
League, Tung Chong Road, Pootung, here we were enlisted
as members and each issued with a membership certificate.

At the beginning of October, the three ex-fitters
above-mentioned put forward demands to the management for
their reinstatement and an increase in wages. These
demands were turned down. On October 18, some 20
planes were stolen from the company premises, and on
October 21, two of the workers were arrested by the Police.
They were interrogated and later released. On October
24, by availing themselves of this excuse, the workers
declared that they were not properly protected and required
the management to reveal the name of the informer. The
management refused to do so, whereupon the workers began
to create trouble. At 9 a.m. that day (October 24,)
the management switched off the machinery and the workers
left the factory. 120 of the workers proceeded to the
League Office on Tung Chong Road, Pootung, by ferry via the

whose factory is situated at 248 Chinwangtao Road, Yangtsepoo
District, are forced to go on strike as from October 24th owing
to the oppressive measures introduced by the Management.
Particulars of the strike are given hereunder and we expect
the public to extend sympathy and help to us.

During June, we were compelled to claim an increase
of 20% as we were unable to make both ends meet due to the
prevailing high cost of living, but the Management refused to
entertain our demand. However, after repeated requests, we
were each given 20 cents extra per day as a rice allowance.
Meanwhile, the Management promised to raise the allowance when
the price of rice increased to $25 and $30 per "Zar". The
Management did not keep the promise when the price of rice
increased to over $40 per "zar". We again requested the
Management to give the increase of the rice allowance favourable
consideration, but our request was ignored. From this we
began to understand that the Management had no mercy on their
labourers.

During August, the wages of our fellow-workers
working in the Engineering Department, Packing Department and
Godown were increased by 25% and we, working in the Machinery
Department, received no increase. We were at a loss to under-
stand this and we had every reason to expect a similar increase
in wages. Instead of giving us an affirmative answer, the
Management dispensed with the services of four laborers
immediately and later dismissed fifteen on different occasions.

The Management accused these dismissed labourers of

机械部全体工人。

我们，利德尔兄弟有限公司（英商）的劳工，工厂位于杨树浦区秦皇岛路248号，由于管理层采取压迫措施，被迫自10月24日起罢工。罢工详情列于下方，我们期望公众给予我们同情和帮助。

6月期间，由于生活成本高涨，我们无法维持生计，被迫要求加薪20%，但管理层拒绝考虑我们的要求。然而，经过反复请求，我们每人每天额外获得20分作为米贴。同时，管理层承诺当米价涨至每“担”25元和30元时，将提高津贴。当米价涨至每“担”40元以上时，管理层并未信守承诺。我们再次请求管理层对增加米贴一事予以有利考虑，但我们的请求被忽视。由此我们开始明白，管理层对他们的劳工毫无怜悯之心。

8月期间，在工程部、包装部和仓库工作的同事工资增加了25%，而我们在机械部工作的人却没有增加。我们对此感到困惑，我们有充分理由期待类似的加薪。管理层没有给我们肯定的答复，反而立即解雇了四名劳工，随后又分批解雇了十五名。

管理层指控这些被解雇的劳工为

being agitators and asserted that the labourers' union, organized
by our fellow-workers, was influenced by the Japanese, whereas,
in fact, the 15 ex-workers are loyal to the Management and the
main purposes of the Labourers' Union are (1) to encourage the
cooperation between labour and capital (2) to effect mutual aid
(3) to promote friendship. From the latter we can see that apart
from the difficulties outlined, the ex-workers have no desire to
cause agitation or to engage themselves in evil-doing. As
regards the accusation that "The Labourers' Union is at the
service of Japanese", we wish to make it clear that we are now
working in the area under the garrison of our Japanese soldier
friends and of course they are sympathetic and protect us. During
the establishment of a new order in East Asia, we should keep in
close contact with our good neighbour Japan in order to reach the
goal - Peace in the Orient and Sino-Japanese Cooperation, and then
we will be safe to enjoy our business. The Management does not
appreciate our ideals and are taking oppressive measures against
us.
On October 19, twenty steel files were missing and
the chief, Tsu Chi Sing (朱啟新) and Zung Tsang Ling (陳璋林),
foreman, submitted a malicious report to the Police. At about
3 p.m. October 23, two laborers, one named Sung Kuo Ziang (沈國祥)
and the other named Liu Pac Tsang (劉保章) were taken to a
special room by the Police where they were interrogated and
tortured and subsequently released for lack of evidence. In view
of this malicious accusation and many other incidents in the past
few months, we protested to the Management on October 24th when
the Management stopped all the machinery and said "Those who wish
to work, say so, otherwise leave the premises immediately." Under
these circumstances, we cannot but to resort to a strike. We shall
be most grateful if the public, Japanese soldier friends and the
City Government will extend to us sympathy and a helping hand.

煽动者，并声称由我们同事组织的劳工工会受日本人影响，而事实上，这15名前工人忠于管理层，劳工工会的主要目的是（1）鼓励劳资合作（2）实行互助（3）促进友谊。从后者可以看出，除了上述困难外，前工人们无意制造煽动或从事恶行。关于“劳工工会为日本人服务”的指控，我们要澄清的是，我们现在在日本军朋友驻防的区域工作，当然他们同情并保护我们。在建立东亚新秩序的过程中，我们应该与好邻居日本保持密切联系，以达到目标——东方和平与中日合作，这样我们才能安全地享受我们的生计。管理层不欣赏我们的理想，并对我们采取压迫措施。
10月19日，二十把钢锉失踪，领班朱启新（Tsu Chi Sing）和陈璋林（Zung Tsang Ling）向警方提交了恶意报告。10月23日下午3时许，两名劳工，一名叫沈国祥（Sung Kuo Ziang），另一名叫刘保章（Liu Pac Tsang），被警察带到一个特别房间，在那里他们受到讯问和酷刑，随后因证据不足被释放。鉴于这一恶意指控以及过去几个月发生的许多其他事件，我们于10月24日向管理层抗议，当时管理层停止了所有机器，并称“愿意工作的就说，否则立即离开工厂。”在这种情况下，我们不得不诉诸罢工。如果公众、日本军朋友和市政府能向我们伸出同情和援助之手，我们将不胜感激。

INDUSTRIAL DISPUTE

Some 290 workers and apprentices employed by Casa-
blanca Factory of Liddell Brothers and Company, Ltd., 248
Yangtszepoo Road, declared a strike in order to enforce the
following demands:

1. That an increase of 25' in wages be granted to all
other workers as those in the engine and packing
rooms.

2. That fifteen workers who have been dismissed by
the management be reinstated.

3. That the dismissed workers be paid full wages
during the period of discharging.

The cause of the strike was that about in the middle
of September, 1939 the management has dismissed some eleven
workers, fitters and machine operators. Therefore the dismissed
workers have persuaded all other workers to strike in sympathy
over their dismissal. A written request has been submitted by
Labour Union of Liddell Brothers & Co., on October 2, 1939, to
the Factory Manager, Mr. Chu Chi Hsing, asking the above
mentioned demands. The workers have first approached the
Chinese Workers' Welfare Association ( 中華工人福利會 ) and
then got the support of the Chinese National Labour Union
( 中華工人同盟會 ) at Pootung representative of the late
organization has called on the management for mediation, but no
result has been received.

After a theft of twenty steel piles, the management
reported to the Police and two suspects, named Liu Pao Tsang
( 刘宝章 ) and Shen Kwoh Tsiang ( 沈国祥 ) were brought to the
Police Station for investigation on October 23. Therefore the
workers declared a strike next morning.

I called on Mr. R. W. Fraser, Manager of Casablanca
Factory, 248 Yangtszepoo Road, this afternoon, October 26, for
investigation. Mr. Fraser stated that some 93 workers resumed work
to-day and hopes more will come to-morrow. He said that the
management has already granted an increase of 15 cents per day to
all the workers from July 1st, 1939, another increase of 5 cents
per day on August 1, and the privilege of having cheap rice sold
to them ½ of "zar" per month at $20 per picul. Therefore the
management, he continued, has treated the workers better than other
factories and if the bad elements agitating the strike were
dismissed, expected the factory to work peacefully.

劳资纠纷

受雇于杨树浦路248号利德尔兄弟有限公司卡萨布兰卡工厂的约290名工人和学徒宣布罢工，以强制实施以下要求：

1. 所有其他工人应像引擎室和包装室的工人一样，获得25%的工资增加。

2. 被管理层解雇的十五名工人应复职。

3. 被解雇的工人在解雇期间应获得全额工资。

罢工的原因是，大约在1939年9月中旬，管理层解雇了约十一名工人、装配工和机器操作员。因此，被解雇的工人说服所有其他工人出于同情他们的解雇而罢工。利德尔兄弟有限公司工会于1939年10月2日向工厂经理朱启星（Chu Chi Hsing）先生提交了一份书面请求，提出上述要求。工人们首先接触了中华工人福利会，然后获得了浦东中华工人同盟会的支持，该后期组织的代表曾拜访管理层进行调解，但未取得结果。

在二十根钢桩被盗后，管理层向警方报告，两名嫌疑人，名为刘宝章（Liu Pao Tsang）和沈国祥（Shen Kwoh Tsiang），于10月23日被带到警察局进行调查。因此，工人们于次日早晨宣布罢工。

今天下午，10月26日，我拜访了杨树浦路248号卡萨布兰卡工厂经理R. W. Fraser先生进行调查。Fraser先生表示，今天约有93名工人复工，希望明天会有更多人回来。他说，管理层已从1939年7月1日起给所有工人每天加薪15分，8月1日又每天加薪5分，并享有每月以每担20元的价格购买半“担”廉价米的特权。因此，他继续说，管理层对待工人比其他工厂更好，如果解雇煽动罢工的不良分子，预计工厂将平静运作。

Warning letters from the Labour Union were sent to workers,
only 40 of whom, therefore, came to work to-day. Two men
attempting picketting were arrested by Police.

The men are ready to give the Union a chance to achieve
something for them, and wait till Monday. Failing action
